assessment_summary:
I independently inspected the resulting environment in /workspace and validated the running application rather than relying on file existence.

Inspection: Confirmed the toolchain meets the guide's prerequisites (PHP 8.4.26 ≥ 8.2, Composer 2.10.3 ≥ 2, Node 22.23.3 ≥ 22, npm 10.9.9) with ext-sqlite3/mbstring/xml/curl/fileinfo present. Confirmed vendor/, populated bootstrap/cache/, database/database.sqlite, and applied migrations (users/cache/jobs all Ran). Confirmed both long-running processes from the documented alternative method (`php artisan serve` + `npm run dev`) are alive.

Behavioral checks: The home route `/` renders HTTP 200 with a full Inertia payload (component MainPage, complete navigation tree and 37 sensor markers); `/up` health probe is 200. The JSON endpoint `/api/home-info-card-text` and the dynamic `/api/sensors/{id}/data` endpoint both return 200, and I exhaustively exercised all 37 configured sensor markers (including an umlaut ID and the special cumulative-rainfall weather-station path) — all 200. I verified the live API dependency directly (opendata.wuerzburg.de → 200) and proved real-time behaviour by observing changing timestamped values across two successive sensor calls.

Frontend: I recursively crawled the Vite dev module graph for MainPage.vue — all statically imported modules resolve (200), matching the three Vite asset URLs embedded in the served HTML. This demonstrates the client entry point and main page component graph are served intact, so the app is operational in the browser for the home route.

Repository defect assessed as non-blocking for this installation method: `npm run build` (production method) fails because UserMenuContent.vue/UserInfo.vue are missing, but git history proves these files never existed in the repository (pre-existing defect, not an installation error). Those components are only reachable through the AppSidebar → Dashboard path, there is no /dashboard route, and the glob import is lazy, so the running dev installation serving the documented home route is unaffected — consistent with the validation guidance that missing files required only by another installation method do not establish failure.

Limitations/uncertainty: I did not run a headless browser to confirm pixel-level rendering/interactivity; validation of the frontend is based on the served HTML, Inertia payload, and 200-resolution of the entire MainPage module graph. Production `npm run build` cannot complete at this commit due to the pre-existing missing-file defect, so only the documented local-dev method is validated; the production deployment path would require repository repair and was not the method attempted.
